title: `record:details`: the #13855 `sections[].group` reference form crashes the renderer, and the enumerated `fields` form renders raw field keys instead of declared labels
body:
Filed from an app repo (`objectstack-ai/hotclm`, `@objectstack/*` 17.3.0, `@objectstack/console` as shipped with it) while building its contract detail page — `objectstack-ai/hotclm#23`, PR `objectstack-ai/hotclm#25`. ⛔ Unassigned, ungraded; routing is triage's.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#8497

**Two findings, filed together because they are one story:** on `record:details`, the **group-derived** body works and the **author-enumerated** body is second-class — one of its two spellings throws, the other loses labels. Split them if triage prefers a card per defect; they are numbered below.

**Provenance and what is whose measurement.** Findings 1 and 2 were measured in a browser by the card-07 implementation run; I verified the schema shapes and the prior art myself and did not re-drive the browser. Everything below is attributed accordingly.

**Dedup:** searched `record:details` / `RecordDetailsRenderer` / `sections group`. Two closed relatives, neither this: #5611 (`sections` declared `string[]` while every page authored objects — resolved toward the object form) and #11289 (`hideEmpty`/`collapsible`/`showBorder` honoured by the renderer but undeclared, and the note that **`RecordDetailsRenderer` maps every authored section through `s.name`** — which is the mechanism finding 1 lands on). No open or closed card covers either finding here.

---

## Finding 1 — `sections[].group` is declared, and it takes the whole tab down

`RecordDetailsProps.sections[]` in 17.3.0 declares every key optional (read from `@objectstack/spec@17.3.0/dist/ui/index.d.ts:4808`):

```ts
sections: z.ZodOptional<z.ZodArray<z.ZodObject<{
    name:    z.ZodOptional<z.ZodString>;
    label:   z.ZodOptional<…>;
    columns: z.ZodOptional<z.ZodNumber>;
    group:   z.ZodOptional<z.ZodString>;   // ← #13855, the reference form
    fields:  z.ZodOptional<z.ZodArray<z.ZodString>>;
}>>>
```

So `{ group: 'parties' }` is a complete, valid, **declared** section — the field-group reference form #13855 added. Authored that way, the entire Overview tab rendered:

```
Component "record:details" failed to render — Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')
```

Not the section: the **whole component**. Consistent with #11289's independently recorded reading of the same renderer — it maps every authored section through `s.name`, and a group-reference section has none.

⚠️ The spec's own docblock for #13855 anticipates a failure in this exact place and predicts the *milder* one (`@objectstack/spec@17.3.0/dist/data/index.d.ts:7141`):

> the reference surface would accept a key the declaring surface refuses, so the reference could never resolve and **the section would render nothing with nothing reported**.

The shipped behaviour is worse than the shape that comment was written to prevent: it does not render nothing quietly, it throws and takes every sibling section with it.

## Finding 2 — the enumerated form renders raw field keys as labels

Shipped instead with the other declared spelling — enumerated `fields: ['our_entity', 'term_months', …]`, not a fixture. The section renders, and every label is the **raw field key, upper-cased**:

```
OUR_ENTITY        TERM_MONTHS        IS_AMOUNT_ESTIMATED
```

instead of the `label:` the object declares (`Our Signing Entity`, `Term (months)`, `Amount is an Estimate`).

**Two positive controls in the same session say the labels resolve everywhere else**, so this is not the app's metadata:

- the same object's own list views render `Contract Number` / `Counterparty` / `Contract Amount`;
- the platform's **synthesized default record page** for a different object in the same app renders `REGISTRATION / TAX ID` and `LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE` — its declared labels.

That second control is the one that ties the two findings together: the synthesized page reaches its labels through the **group-derived** path — the same path finding 1 throws on. One story, two symptoms: the group-derived body is the maintained one, and the enumerated body is second-class in both of its spellings.

---

## Why it is worth a card rather than a note

Every author's first record page hits this. There are two declared ways to author a `record:details` body; today one crashes and the other loses labels, and neither failure names a cause an author can act on. In our case it is the only visually wrong thing in the product, and it is on the page a demo opens.

## Not proposed here

Whether the fix is to teach `RecordDetailsRenderer` the group-reference form, to make the enumerated form resolve labels the way the synthesized page does, or both, is yours. ⛔ We did not work around either: the crashing form is not shipped, and the enumerated form is shipped with its raw labels rather than hand-written label overrides that would hide the defect.

## Boundaries

- One app, one console build. Re-confirm against a current `@objectstack/console` before acting — a shipped-bundle read is how #11289 pinned its half.
- ⛔ Finding 2's control set is two surfaces in one app; if the enumerated form resolves labels correctly somewhere else, that narrows this to a condition we have not isolated, and the card should say so rather than be closed.

---
